command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# PATH export IS needed here: aarchbio images have their PATH dropped by the task shell.
# (aarchsci env images are the opposite -- exporting there shadows their python, which cost
# two dead runs on the gsw recipe.)
#
# This task generates the fileset ONCE and stages it, so the PLINK 2 task reads the same
# BYTES rather than regenerating from the same seed. The cross-check rule is explicit: point
# the second tool at the first one's staged input, because a second generation is a second
# thing to keep true.

plink --version | head -1

echo "== generate a deterministic fileset: 300 samples, 1000 variants, 2% missing =="
plink --dummy 300 1000 0.02 0 acgt --seed 42 --make-bed --out data > /tmp/gen.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -20 /tmp/gen.log; echo "FAIL: --dummy failed"; exit 1; }
ls -l data.bed data.bim data.fam | awk '{print "file\t"$9"\t"$5}'
sha256sum data.bed data.bim data.fam | tee data.sha256

echo "== allele counts, missingness, HWE =="
plink --bfile data --freq counts --out p19 > /tmp/freq.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/freq.log; exit 1; }
plink --bfile data --missing        --out p19 > /tmp/miss.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/miss.log; exit 1; }
plink --bfile data --hardy          --out p19 > /tmp/hwe.log  2>&1 || { cat /tmp/hwe.log;  exit 1; }

head -2 p19.frq.counts | sed 's/^/  frq: /'
head -2 p19.lmiss      | sed 's/^/  lmiss: /'
head -2 p19.hwe        | sed 's/^/  hwe: /'

# Normalise to a convention-free summary. A1 in PLINK 1.9 is the MINOR allele; PLINK 2 reports
# the ALT allele instead, so "A1 count" vs "ALT count" would compare two different things.
# min(count, total-count) is the minor-allele count under either convention, and it is an
# INTEGER -- so the comparison can be exact equality rather than a tolerance.
awk 'NR>1{t=$5+$6; m=($5<$6?$5:$6); print $2"\t"m"\t"t}' p19.frq.counts | sort -k1,1 > p19.minor.tsv
awk 'NR>1{print $2"\t"$3"\t"$4}' p19.lmiss | sort -k1,1 > p19.miss.tsv
# PLINK 1.9's --hardy emits THREE rows per variant (TEST = ALL / AFF / UNAFF) whenever a
# case/control phenotype exists, and --dummy creates one. PLINK 2 emits a single all-samples
# row. Without this filter the later strata silently overwrite ALL when keyed by variant ID,
# and the comparison becomes PLINK 1.9's UNAFF subset against PLINK 2's whole sample --
# measured at 9.2e-01 apart, which reads as a catastrophic disagreement and is really a
# different population. Restrict to ALL so the two sides are the same samples.
awk 'NR>1 && $3=="ALL"{print $2"\t"$9}' p19.hwe | sort -k1,1 > p19.hwe.tsv
awk 'NR>1{print $3}' p19.hwe | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/^/  hwe TEST strata present: /'
echo
wc -l p19.minor.tsv p19.miss.tsv p19.hwe.tsv | sed 's/^/  /'

echo "PLINK19 OK"
